metas.name: Car Meta - Manu'a Car
metas.note: The front of a silver-grey truck with side mirrors can be seen on Manu’a and Olosega, which are connected by a bridge.

metas.name: Car Meta - Tau Car
metas.note: The front of a similar truck can be seen on the easternmost covered island of Tau. However, the truck will be glossy black, with side mirrors visible.

metas.name: Car Meta - Tutuila Car
metas.note:
A slightly rusted black truck bed can be seen on the main island of Tutuila.

This is the most common car that will be seen as it has the most coverage.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Bridge
metas.note: The single-lane bridge, connecting the islands of Manu’a and Olosega, can be easily recognized by the thin wire guardrail, with the two islands on either side of the bridge.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Coconut / Powerline / Guardrail
metas.note:
Tau has a long East-West road that is difficult to line up.

If you're generally heading East-West, have Concrete Pavement and you see a lot of Coconut Palms, you're in the central part of the road, east of the river.

The short stretch immediately east of the river only shows the Coconuts in the distance towards East. There's both a Powerline and a Guardrail.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Manu'a/Olosega Sand Road
metas.note:
From slightly North of the town entry of Olosega until the southernmost house WEST of the road, you will have a plain sand road, with no grass verge in the middle.

This is the only road of this kind on the two islands with this Google Car.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Ofu Airport
metas.note: Ofu Airport is small with a concrete runway. The Google Car covering it has two orange straps on the roof. Many palm trees can also be seen on the other side of the runway.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Super Straight Road
metas.note: This section of the Rte 014 is by far the straightest covered road on Tutuila. Use the road angle to confirm. The appearance is quite varied, but it's also very flat

metas.name: Infrastructure - Tau - Asphalt
metas.note:
Tau has a long East-West road that is difficult to line up.

If you're generally heading East-West and have Asphalt pavement, you're on the far west part of the road.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Tau - Coconut / No Powerline
metas.note:
Tau has a long East-West road that is difficult to line up.

If you're generally heading East-West, have Concrete Pavement and you see a lot of Coconut Palms, you're in the central part of the road, east of the river.

The short stretch immediately east of the little sideroad has no powerline, unlike the other locs with Coconuts.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Tau - Coconut / Powerline / No Guardrail
metas.note:
Tau has a long East-West road that is difficult to line up.

If you're generally heading East-West, have Concrete Pavement and you see a lot of Coconut Palms, you're in the central part of the road, east of the river.

On this stretch, if you have a powerline, but no guardrail, you're east of the river, and west of the small sideroad on the map.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Tau - Concrete / Overgrown / Guardrail / No Powerline
metas.note:
Tau has a long East-West road that is difficult to line up.

If you're generally heading East-West, have Concrete Pavement and a lot of overgrowth between you and the coast, you're generally in the Western Part of the road.

If additionally, you have a guardrail, but no powerline, you're on the east-west stretch west of the river.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Tau - Concrete / Overgrown / No Guardrail
metas.note:
Tau has a long East-West road that is difficult to line up.

If you're generally heading East-West, have Concrete Pavement and a lot of overgrowth between you and the coast, you're generally in the Western Part of the road.

If additionally, you have no guardrail, you're on the stretch marked on the second image, south of a smooth coast protrusion west of the river.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Tau - Overgrown - Powerline
metas.note:
Tau has a long East-West road that is difficult to line up.

If you're generally heading East-West, have Concrete Pavement and a lot of overgrowth between you and the coast, you're generally in the Western Part of the road.

If additionally, you have a powerline visible, you're on the SW-NE stretch immediately west of the river.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Tau - Visible Coast / Guardrail
metas.note:
Tau has a long East-West road that is difficult to line up.

If you're generally heading East-West, have Concrete Pavement and you have the coast North of you, with no significant vegetation in the way, you're on the Easternmost part of the road, east of the little sideroad.

The western half of this stretch has a guardrail, the eastern half does not.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Tau - Visible Coast / No Guardrail
metas.note:
Tau has a long East-West road that is difficult to line up.

If you're generally heading East-West, have Concrete Pavement and you have the coast North of you, with no significant vegetation in the way, you're on the Easternmost part of the road, east of the little sideroad.

The western half of this stretch has a guardrail, the eastern half does not.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Tutuila Airport
metas.note: On the roads along the airport on Tutuila, you will always see these fences surrounding the airport. This is obviously common for airports, but since Tutuila only has one airstrip, this road is a free 5k together with the Tutuila car.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Tutuila Concrete Road
metas.note: If you are on Tutuila and have a Concrete Road with no coast visible, you're on the far Eastern Part of the island, between Onenoa and Matatula Elementary school.

metas.name: Landscape - Afono Bay
metas.note: Afono Bay is the only Bay with coverage that is opened towards straight North. Note that Fagasa Bay is opened towards Northwest, while Vatia Bay is opened towards Northeast.

metas.name: Landscape - Camel Rock
metas.note:
Behold: The Camel Rock. Two little peaks reaching into the ocean.

It is marked as a POI on Google Maps.

metas.name: Landscape - East of Summit 001 - Overcast
metas.note:
This road crosses the district border on the 001. It is characterized through the unique angle and the mountains in the north. Often you can see a unique summit in the west. The driving direction is eastwards.

There is a stretch of the 001 with a similar angle near Malaeimi, but it has a clearly visible valley in the North which is not found on this road.

The road can further be divided as it is overcast in the Western District and sunny in the Eastern District.

metas.name: Landscape - East of Summit 001 - Sunny
metas.note:
This road crosses the district border on the 001. It is characterized through the unique angle and the mountains in the north. Often you can see a unique summit in the west. The driving direction is eastwards.

There is a stretch of the 001 with a similar angle near Malaeimi, but it has a clearly visible valley in the North which is not found on this road.

The road can further be divided as it is overcast in the Western District and sunny in the Eastern District.

metas.name: Landscape - Eastern South Coast Road
metas.note:
This long stretch of road (which is probably further regionguessable) is easily recognizable because it has a South Coast and the Car Drives westward (unlike the Western Coastal Road). That means that when you pan onto the back of the truck, the water will be to your right.

There is one annoying exception, around the POI 'Amouli Beach Fales' east of the town Amouli.

metas.name: Landscape - Fagasa Bay
metas.note: Afono Bay is the only Bay with coverage that is opened towards Northwest. Note that Afono is opened towards North proper, while Vatia Bay is opened towards Northeast.

metas.name: Landscape - Manu'a - North Coast road (paved)
metas.note: On Manu'a/Olosega (which have a unique car), there are two covered roads with North coast: The roads east and west of the famous bridge. They can easily be differentiated, because the Olosega (east) road is unpaved, while the Manu'a (west) road has concrete pavement.

metas.name: Landscape - Manu'a - North Coast road (unpaved)
metas.note: On Manu'a/Olosega (which have a unique car), there are two covered roads with North coast: The roads east and west of the famous bridge. They can easily be differentiated, because the Olosega (east) road is unpaved, while the Manu'a (west) road has concrete pavement.

metas.name: Landscape - Manu'a - Ofu
metas.note:
The town Ofu on Manu'a has a West Coast. This road can be distinguished from the West Coast of Olosega, because:

  • It is entirely paved (unlike the town Olosega)
  • It has no Mountain in the North (unlike the paved road north of Olosega).

metas.name: Landscape - Pago Pago Harbour
metas.note: The roads alonog the Pago Pago Harbour are recognizable because they're generally very urban (for American Samoa), and you can often see the harbour when it isn't blocked by buildings.

metas.name: Landscape - Tau - Faleasao
metas.note: Faleasao is a little town on Tau (and thus has the Tau car). It has a coast in the North and is otherwise surrounded by mountains. Together with the Tau car, it is unique.

metas.name: Landscape - Tutuila - Rte 018
metas.note:
The Rte 018 in Tafuna is urban and uniquely shows this mountain in the North. The alignment is generally North-South. The road has double yellow lines (not that common in AS) and a power line in the East. The driving direction is to the North.

Make sure that parts of the Rte 001 can look similar with a similar road angle. To confirm it's the Rte 018, you can pan exactly North. If you look at the mountain, it's the Rte 018, otherwise it's not.

metas.name: Landscape - Tutuila East Coast
metas.note: This is the only part of Tutuila where you can see Coast on the east, without other parts of Tutuila visible. You will often see Aunu'u in the Southeast.

metas.name: Landscape - Vatia Bay
metas.note: Vatia Bay is the only Bay with coverage that is opened towards Northeast. Note that Fagasa Bay is opened towards Northwest, while Afono Bay is opened towards North proper.

metas.name: Landscape - Western South Coast Road
metas.note:
This road is easily recognizable because it has a South Coast and the Car drives eastward (unlike the Eastern Coastal Road). That means that when you pan onto the back of the truck, the water will be to your left.

On the eastern south coast road, there is a tiny part that also drives eastward for some reason, which can be baity.

metas.name: Trekker - Aunu Ferry
metas.note: The only ferry Trekker of American Samoa. If you're on a boat between two islands in AS, you're here.

metas.name: Trekker - Ofu Beach
metas.note: Ofu Beach is easy to recognize, with the coast to the Southeast and three distinct peaks in the Northeast.
